question: Should the 1,280 mirrored SEBI Scheme Information Documents be committed?
why_it_is_not_obvious: .gitignore says plainly that source documents in documents/ ARE committed — 'that is the point of them, so a published fact can be checked against the document it was read from'. By that rule these belong in the repo. But the SIDs are 1.4 GB against a .git already at 726 MB, so committing them takes the repository past 2 GB and changes what cloning it costs anyone. The 30 tracked funds documents today are factsheets, not SIDs.
what_depends_on_them: 5,700 committed fund facts were read from these documents this session — exit_load_note on 2,995 records, benchmark on 2,683, lock_in_months on 22. Every one cites its SID. Without the documents in the repo those citations point at files only this machine holds.

options.commit_them: Honours the stated rule and makes every citation checkable. Repo goes past 2 GB.
options.commit_a_manifest_only: documents.json per scheme already records the SEBI URL and a hash. SEBI serves these publicly and permits crawling, so a reader can re-fetch. Cheap, but a dead URL breaks the audit trail — and 12 of 15 MITC URLs in this repo have already died.
options.git_lfs: Keeps the files addressable without the pack cost; adds a dependency and a store.

recovered_today: 27 of these PDFs were truncated downloads with damaged xref tables — valid %PDF headers, no %%EOF. All 27 were re-fetched from the SEBI URLs in their manifests and now extract 8,486-27,044 characters where they previously yielded nothing. Two needed a second attempt after transient TLS handshake errors.
not_decided_here: Repository shape is the owner's call, not a data fix. Left untracked.
